<reason>PRO won the central access clash and the comparison. Its peer-supplier mechanism — 18-year-olds supplying 16-year-old classmates, removed only when no school cohort can ever buy legally and the legal pool only shrinks — was conceded as an advantage by CON, while CON's resale and inequality objections apply as much or more to 21-only rules that refill legal youth buyers every year. CON kept a valid proportionality worry but never solved the replenishment problem.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Rebuttal 1 peer-bridge response: teen supply is barely-legal friends, not cartels, so a cutoff creates an aging gap outside the peer group and the legal pool shrinks through quitting/death instead of replenishing.</best_rebuttal>
